data.name: Qaim
data.long_meaning: One who is established or upright in his faith and deeds, fulfilling his responsibilities and duties.
data.spiritual_meaning: In the Quran, Qaim refers to the Last Prophet, Muhammad (peace be upon him), who will be the first to rise from the dead on the Day of Judgment.
data.numerology_meaning: A strong, independent, and creative soul, who needs to be in control of their own destiny

in_arabic.name: قائم
in_arabic.long_meaning: قائم هو اسم عربي مشتق من الفعل قام الذي يعني القيام أو الوقوف، ويشير إلى الشخص الذي يقوم بشيء أو يحققه، وله أهمية دينية وثقافية في الإسلام حيث يوصف به الإمام المهدي في الاعتقاد الشيعي

in_urdu.name: قائم
in_urdu.long_meaning: قائم کا مطلب ہے کھڑا ہونے والا یا قیام کرنے والا، یہ نام عرب سے ماخوذ ہے اور اس کی اہمیت شیعہ عقیدے میں امام مہدی کے ساتھ منسلک ہے

in_hindi.name: क़ाएम
in_hindi.long_meaning: क़ाएम का अर्थ है खड़ा होने वाला या उठने वाला, यह नाम अरबी से आया है और इसका महत्व शिया विश्वास में इमाम महदी के साथ जुड़ा हुआ है

in_pashto.name: قائم
in_pashto.long_meaning: قائم د پوها د چالو یا پورته کيدو څخه معنا لري، دا نوم عرب څخه راوړل شوی دی او د شيعو عقيدې کې د امام مهدي سره تړلی دی

in_english.name: Qaim
in_english.meaning: the one who rises or stands
in_english.long_meaning: Qaim means the one who rises or stands, derived from the Arabic root q-w-m, it refers to a person who establishes or upholds something, and has religious significance in Islam, particularly in Shia belief as a title for Imam Mahdi

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Qaim' holds a significant cultural value in the Islamic society as it symbolizes righteousness, strength, and leadership. The belief in an Imam Mahdi, the awaited leader and savior of the Muslim Ummah, who will re-establish justice and peace on earth, stems from this name. The title of Qaim is attributed to this promised leader, reinforcing the idea of striving for virtuous leadership and upholding faith and moral values in the community.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Qaim signifies a deep connection to one's faith and commitment to leading an upright and moral life. It not only implies the fulfillment of religious obligations but also emphasizes the importance of personal responsibility, resilience, and character in conforming to the divine will. The Arabic root-words emphasize the constant striving for progress and growth, both inwardly as well as outwardly, as key elements of Islamic spirituality.
